title: The Spark: Fort Sumter

segments.text: The first shot of the Civil War hit a fort in Charleston harbour.
It is half past four in the morning, April twelfth, eighteen sixty-one.
Confederate guns open fire on Fort Sumter, held by United States soldiers.
Inside, about eighty men and a few civilians take cover.
Remarkably, nobody on either side is killed by the shelling.
The garrison surrenders, and the flag comes down.
Within days, President Lincoln calls for seventy-five thousand volunteers.
Four more states leave the Union to join the Confederacy.
Both sides think it will be over in weeks.
People even brought picnics to watch the first big battle that summer.
Instead, it will last four years.

verify: Fort Sumter bombardment: 12-13 April 1861; garrison ~85 (Anderson: 85 officers/men); no combat deaths from bombardment (verify; a gun accident killed one during surrender salute); Lincoln 75,000 on 15 Apr; VA, AR, TN, NC joined
